newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Howard Smith says on track for strong H2.
newsitem.headline: Howard Smith says on track for strong H2.

text.p: Hardware, engineering and towage group Howard Smith Ltd said on Thursday it was on track for its forecast of a strong profit rise in the second half of 1996/97 (July/June).
Managing director Ken Moss told reporters in Melbourne he expected profit for the second half-year to be similar to the the first half-year.
In February, Howard Smith reported a better-than-expected net profit after abnormals of A$61.3 million, a 56.8 percent rise on the first half-year of 1995/96.
"I think our first-half result is pretty well a fair indication of how we are going," Moss said. "There's nothing that's changed our view on that."
Moss repeated earlier remarks that Howard Smith was comfortable with independent forecasts of a full year profit before abnormals of about A$95 million.
"The market is probably looking for around A$95 million...and we would not argue with that," he said after addressing the Securuties Institute of Australia.
Howard Smith reported a net profit of A$86.13 million in 1995/96, including a pre-tax abnormal profit of A$3.48 million.
Howard Smith expects its BBC hardware division to fuel much of the profit growth in the second half-year, with its engineering and towage divisions also contributing strongly.

The BBC hardware chain, bought from Burns Philp and Co Ltd for A$460 million in 1994, now reaps annual sales of A$1.1 billion and has become Howard Smith's major earnings driver since its withdrawal from non-towage shipping operations.
Moss said BBC was aggressively building market share in retail hardware, establishing a growing network of big warehouse-style outlets in inner-city areas around Australia.
The emphasise on retail sales fattens profit margins and gives Howard Smith some protection from Australia's prolonged downturn in the construction industry, he said.
Howard Smith has 17 of its so-called "Hardwarehouse" stores around Australia and plans to open another 23 by the end of calendar 1998, each at a cost of A$20 million including stock.
BBC accounts for 35 percent of Howard Smith's earnings before interest and tax, but has only seven percent of Australia's A$15 billion hardware market, Moss said.
"We see us being in a position of taking a lot more market share than we have at the moment," he said in his speech.
The additional market share will come at the expense of "the weak and the defenceless" -- small hardware stores, such as the franchise operations run under the Mitre 10 banner, Moss said.
Howard Smith is also eyeing possible acquisitions in Australia and offshore, Moss said
In Australia, it is looking to buy specialist businesses to expand the product range of its Blackwoods industrial hardware business, which services the construction and mining industries.
Offshore, it is looking at towage opportunities in continental Europe and Asia. "We are interested in opportunities but we will be very selective," Moss said.
A share buy-back would only be considered if Howard Smith found itself under-geared and unable to find suitable acquisitions, he added.
-- Melbourne bureau 613-9286-1421
